subject.title: Feature Request: Abstract file scanning pipeline as Memory Plugin API

question: Should OpenClaw add a public host-delivered memory file-ingestion API for active memory plugins, or keep scan/watch/hash-diff/stale-cleanup ownership inside each memory backend/plugin?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but delivering local memory files and extraPaths contents to plugin code changes the public SDK contract and sensitive local-file trust boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrow SDK design first
options.body: Design and approve a minimal memory ingestion capability with explicit security, compatibility, and test requirements before implementation.

options.title: Keep scanning plugin-owned
options.body: Document that memory plugins may use current list/read helpers but must own their own watchers, indexing, deletion, and cleanup behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader memory backend design
options.body: Defer this issue until a broader memory backend/provider contract also decides file ingestion, search, get, writeback, and status ownership.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow SDK design first
recommendation.body: Design and approve a minimal memory ingestion capability with explicit security, compatibility, and test requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across memory SDK helpers, docs, and memory plugin boundary work.
